What has been your experience with the lifespan of hard disk drives?

Worst for me: Hitachi DeathDeskstar. I haven't used one in 10 forever's.

Current: 1 Seagate 1TB, 3 WD 300G,150G, 100G. The SG is newish (last may?) and the 3 others were from my old setup. I don't have the age on them because I swap drives quite a bit.

Oldest: Hard to tell, I have a ton of old parts. I think I have a Quantum Bigfoot laying around as a wall hanger. Willing to bet it's toast by now.

Case cooling was an issue with my old Aspire X-Cruiser so I moved up a few months ago to a Thermaltake Core v21. Not a lot of room for securing down the drives along with cramming a optical in it (mounted to the internal bottom). When I replace the WDs I'll be getting one or two 2.5"ers. For now, zip-ties.

I don't have any empirical data, but 2.5" drives I typically get about 2-4 years. For 3.5" form factor I got 3-4 years out of IBM Deskstars, before they had problems. Post Death-star era been mostly using Western Digital. WD 120G, 250G, 500G (pre-color code/types) lasted me 5-7 years. I keep my desktop system always on and plugged into UPS -- personally I believe UPS extends the life span of my computer components.

My oldest was a 7 year old 500G WD, which failed me a couple of months ago. In general, my personal metric: if the HD has a 3-year warranty, hasn't been dropped, and plugged into a UPS I expect three to five year range, plus-or-minus two years out of a HD. PSA: no matter what your luck has been with drives, if the data is critical to you, back that shit up (different places and drives)!
